problem: The engineNote's proposed implementation does not work, and the note only hedges ("verify choiceGrants is honoured for skillChoices/redundantFallback"). I verified it: in build.ts the choiceGrants entry is merged via `for (const src of [g, fc.choice?.value ? g.choiceGrants?.[fc.choice.value] : undefined])`, and that loop applies ONLY armor / weapon / save / perception / skills / conditionalSkills. `skillChoices` is resolved outside that loop from the top-level grant only — `(g.skillChoices ?? []).forEach(...)` at build.ts:2151 — and `redundantFallback` is explicitly gated to the static grant by `if (g.redundantFallback && src === g && ...)`. weaponFamiliarity is the ONLY choice-dependent extra, handled in its own separate loop. So a choiceGrants entry containing `skillChoices` + `redundantFallback` would be silently ignored, and the style-dependent Acrobatics-or-style-skill option set cannot be expressed today.

Implementing this feat requires EITHER extending build.ts so choiceGrants entries also feed the skillChoices resolver (build.ts:2151) and the redundantFallback branch, OR a dedicated dependent-choice lane. Everything else in the spec is confirmed correct: the six options are exactly d.classes.swashbuckler.subclass.options (battledancer/braggart/fencer/gymnast/rascal/wit), the record has no `choice` field, and featGrantsAuto.ts:287 really is `'swashbuckler-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }` (wrong — offers any skill). problem: The option source is wrong in a way that would match zero items: "content.items filtered to category 'weapon'". In core.json, weapons are identified by `itemType === 'weapon'` (1,039 records); `category` on a weapon item holds the PROFICIENCY tier — I counted simple 308 / martial 633 / advanced 71 / unarmed 6 / ammunition 3 — e.g. items['longsword'] is { itemType: 'weapon', category: 'martial', group: 'sword' }. There is also no `base` field on item records, so "keyed by base-item slug" is only true in the sense that the item id IS the slug.
correction: Filter `itemType === 'weapon'` and store the item id. That id is the right key: derive.ts builds each Strike with `base: w.id` and weaponMatches() tests `strike.base` against `critSpecWeapons.bases`, so the stored pick drops straight into the bases array. Everything else in this spec checks out and is the most valuable finding in the chunk: critSpecWeapons.bases really does contain the literal Foundry placeholder "{actor|flags.system.godlingWeapon}" (dead grant), StrikeDamageRider really has only appliesTo: 'all'|'unarmed'|'melee'|'ranged' (no per-base restriction), and weaponOverrides really is Record<weaponId, ProficiencyRank>, which is the right home for "treat this weapon as a simple weapon for proficiency".

problem: The engineNote's load-bearing claim is false: "zero items in core.json currently carry a choice or effectChoices field, so this would be the first item-driven builder prompt". 29 items already carry effectChoices — energy-robe, eidolon-cape, druids-crown, broadleaf-shield (x4), energy-resistant (x2), charm-of-resistance (x3), entertainers-cincture (x2), wyrms-wingspan (x3), wyrm-on-the-wing (x3), helm-of-zeal-greater, essence-charm, muse, track-of-the-beast, plus 4 aon-* duplicates. types.ts ItemBase documents the field: "'Choose one of N' passive effects (Energy Robe's resistance type)... resolved into resolvedItemPassives when worn". Item-choice wiring (ItemBase.effectChoices -> BuildState.effectChoices keyed <recordId>:<choiceId> -> resolvedItemPassives) already ships and needs no new plumbing. What is actually missing is three narrower things: (1) EffectChoice can express a fixed `options` list or an open `spellFilter`, but has no skill/Lore filter — a free-text-Lore analogue of spellFilter is the natural extension; (2) free-text Lore input already exists TWICE (Background.trainedLoreChoice -> BuildState.backgroundLore, and DefenseGrants.loreChoices -> BuildState.heritageLore) but both grant TRAINED, so the conditional master/legendary-at-15 rank override is the real new capability; (3) the 'a Lore you have no proficiency in' validator and the once-per-day re-pick (daily preparations) still need somewhere to live. The human question should therefore be only 'one-time invest prompt vs daily-prep slot, and enforce-or-warn' — not 'should items be allowed builder prompts at all'.

problem: needsEngineWork:false is wrong. problem: needsEngineWork:false with no engineNote at all is wrong, and the reasonIfNo's claim that Specialty Crafting's choice 'must be prompted there' asserts a prompt that does not happen. feats['specialty-crafting'].choice is present (flag 'specialtyCrafting', 12 options alchemy…woodworking), but as a background grantedFeatId it goes through build.ts:1900-1903 / Builder.tsx:990-1004, which never render a picker and never store a value. problem: The core finding (hardcoded trainedLore) is correct and confirmed — the record really does carry `"trainedLore": "Jungle"` with no trainedLoreChoice, so build.ts:1201 trains it unconditionally and 2 of 3 legal builds are unreachable. problem: The spec's structured fields encode ONLY the branch affiliation (flag magaambyanBranch, picks 1). The record's headline benefit is a different, unrecorded build-time choice: "You gain the ability to cast a single arcane or primal cantrip of your choice... If you weren't already, you become trained in that tradition's spell DCs and spell attack rolls, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability if you choose arcane or Wisdom as your spellcasting ability if you choose primal." correction: Promote this to a MULTI-CHOICE record. (1) PRIMARY — tradition: kind 'array', flag 'halcyonTradition', options [{arcane → spellcastingGrant {tradition:'arcane', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'}}, {primal → {tradition:'primal', keyAbility:'wis', proficiency:'trained'}}]. Feat.spellcastingGrant is a fixed object, so the two options must each carry their own — that IS the engine gap to state. (2) DEPENDENT — cantrip: open pick, SpellChoiceFilter { traditions:[<chosen>], cantripsOnly:true, grantAs:'innate', innate:{ tradition:<chosen>, atWill:true, heightenHalfLevel:true } }; or, to avoid the dependent-pick gap entirely, ship it today as two FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS-style fixed lists (arcane cantrips / primal cantrips) the way arcane-tattoos and wildborn-magic already do. Also correct as the spec says: add conditionalRank {base:'trained', upgraded:'expert'} to FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['magaambyan-attendant-dedication'].skillChoices (verified present in featGrants.ts:92 and used by build.ts:2158, and verified missing from featGrantsAuto.ts:188).

problem: Two errors. (a) needsEngineWork: true is wrong — no engine change is needed. The record can be fixed with data alone by the exact pattern additional-shadow-magic already ships: `effectChoices: [{ id:'school-spell', options: [8 × { value, label, grant:{ focusSpells:[<id>] } }] }]` AND deleting `focusPoolBonus: 1`. FeatChoiceDef (types.ts) is only { flag, prompt, kind:'domains'|'array', options } and an 'array' choice grants NOTHING — build.ts's applyFeatFocus only turns a choice into a focus spell when kind === 'domains' (line 1374). Authoring this as choice.kind 'array' would record a label and grant no spell.

Replace kind:'array' with an effectChoices spec (id 'school-spell', the same 8 options, each option's grant = { focusSpells: [id] }), and state explicitly that `focusPoolBonus: 1` must be REMOVED from the record in the same edit. Option ids verified present in core.json: protective-wards, fortify-summoning, diviners-sight, charming-push, force-bolt, warped-terrain, call-of-the-grave, physical-boost (the legacy slugs protective-ward / augment-summoning / charming-words are indeed absent). problem: The engineNote inverts the actual defect. It claims the top-level `innateSpells: [{spellId:'enlarge', tradition:'primal'}]` is applied IN ADDITION to the chosen option's grant, 'so this feat currently grants Enlarge TWICE'. It does not. build.ts pushes each taken feat's top-level innateSpells at lines 2536-2540, THEN the resolved effect-choice grants (chosenInnateGrants) at 2542-2545, and then dedupes by spellId keeping the FIRST occurrence: `const seenInnate = new Set<string>(); const innate = innateGrants.filter((g) => content.spells[g.spellId] && !seenInnate.has(g.spellId) && seenInnate.add(g.spellId));` (build.ts:2555-2556).
correction: The top-level grant SHADOWS the chosen one — the player's pick is completely inert, not duplicated. Whichever option is selected, the character ends up with a single generic Enlarge cast at its base rank 2 with the default 1/day (castRank at build.ts:2561-2568 sees no `rank`, and usesPerDay defaults to 1 at 2581). So enlarge-2nd loses its 2/day and enlarge-4th loses BOTH its rank-4 and its 1/day distinction. The fix (delete the top-level innateSpells now that effectChoices covers it) is unchanged, but the reported symptom must be 'the choice does nothing' — that is the Assurance failure mode, and it will not be found by looking for a duplicated Spells-page row.

problem: Three defects. problem: Says the record's effectChoices are complete ("Nothing to add", needsEngineWork false) and reports "16 options". problem: engineNote claims "the ten initiate-benefit-<implement> classFeature records exist in core.json but nothing in src/ references them". problem: engineNote says "NOT implemented anywhere … no BuildState field, no effectChoices on the record, and no code path mentions it" and proposes a hand-typed 3-option array, then claims "Blessed Swiftness is nearly expressible via DefenseGrants.landSpeedBonus: 5, except that field is a flat bonus while the text specifies a STATUS bonus". problem: needsHumanDecision is set to false, but this record contains exactly the kind of call the instructions say must be escalated. The text is "You're trained in the Arcana skill and an additional skill in which the clockwork entity is well-versed, DETERMINED BY THE GM." (verified verbatim). The spec silently converts a GM-assigned skill into an unrestricted player pick over all skills, and buries that decision in the 'restriction' prose ('in the app the player records it') rather than surfacing it. Two owner decisions are hidden: (a) whether the builder prompts at all for something RAW hands to the GM, versus leaving it as a note/free-text the player fills in after asking their GM; (b) whether the pool is truly all skills or excludes Arcana and skills already trained from another source — the record gives no guidance, and every other trained-skill grant in the app locks its pick (build.ts:1200 calls locked.add).
correction: Set needsHumanDecision:true with the question: "Mechanical Symbiosis's second trained skill is 'determined by the GM'. Should the builder (a) prompt the player with a full skill picker, (b) prompt with a picker that excludes Arcana and already-trained skills, or (c) not prompt and instead show a note that the GM assigns it? This is the first GM-assigned build-time grant in the data, so it sets precedent." Keep needsBuildChoice:true (the skill must land on the sheet somehow — leaving it unmodelled is the worse bug) and keep needsEngineWork:true. Also note the internal contradiction to fix: the spec sets kind:'skills' while its own engineNote correctly observes that types.ts:527 declares kind as 'domains' | 'array' only — verified, 'skills' does not exist. State it as a proposed new kind, not as if it were available.

Keep needsHumanDecision false.

problem: needsBuildChoice=false rests on a factually false reason. The spec says Alchemical Crafting's "4 common 1st-level alchemical formulas are a DAILY/formula-book matter, not a build-time picker". The feat's own text in core.json says the opposite: feats['alchemical-crafting'].description = "You can use the Craft activity to create alchemical items. When you select this feat, you immediately add the formulas for four common 1st-level alchemical items to your formula book." — "when you select this feat" is build time, and a formula book is permanent, not daily. This also breaks the reviewer's own convention: it marked Ustalavic Academic (grants Skill Training -> pick a skill) and Onyx Trader (grants Multilingual -> pick 2 languages) TRUE precisely because the background-granted feat carries an unresolved sub-choice. Alkenstar Tinker is the same shape (grantedFeatId='alchemical-crafting', feats['alchemical-crafting'].choice is undefined) and was classified the opposite way.
correction: Set needsBuildChoice true (or at minimum replace the reason). chooses: 'other' (alchemical formulas / items); openSource: any COMMON 1st-level item with the alchemical trait — open pool, do not enumerate; picks: 4; effect: adds 4 permanent formulas to the character's formula book. needsEngineWork TRUE: the app has no formula book at all — src/data/transfer.ts:1055-1056 literally comments "Crafting formulas are a known-recipes list, not carried gear — the app has no formula book" and drops imported formulas with a warning (transfer.ts:1108). The existing precedent to copy is SnareFormulasCard (src/builder/shared.tsx:1729-1775), which stores snare-formula picks in build.extraChoices[SNARE_FORMULA_KEY] — an alchemical equivalent would be the same lane. Add needsHumanDecision true: 'does Heroes Heaven want a general formula-book lane, or should Alchemical Crafting stay display-only?' Note this is a shared feat-level gap, not background-specific — every Alchemical Crafting take is affected, not just this background.

problem: Two errors, both in load-bearing parts of the spec. (1) engineNote claim (a) is false: "there is NO feat-driven language lane at all — build.ts:2790-2793 derives language slots solely from max(0,Int mod) + ancestry.languages.additional". The cited range stops three lines short of the contradicting code. src/rules/build.ts:2796 reads `const featLangs = feats.flatMap((fc) => content.feats[fc.featId]?.grantsLanguages ?? [])` and line 2801 unions featLangs (plus heritage and invested-item languages) on top of the Int/ancestry budget. A feat-driven language lane DOES exist. (2) picks:2 is incomplete — feats['multilingual'].description: "You learn two new languages... You learn an additional language if you are or become a master in Society and again if you are or become legendary." A fixed picks:2 under-prompts a master/legendary-Society character by 1-2 languages.
correction: Rewrite engineNote (a) to the actual, much smaller gap: feats carry `grantsLanguages` (a FIXED string list consumed at build.ts:2796) but there is no CHOOSE-N language field, and feats['multilingual'] has no grantsLanguages at all (its keys are only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/description/source/prerequisites/actionCost/maxTakable/edition) — so Multilingual grants nothing today. The fix is a new choose-N language lane (e.g. featLanguageChoices keyed `<featId>:<idx>`, mirroring build.featSkillChoices) merged in alongside featLangs at build.ts:2796-2801 — not a language subsystem from scratch. Change picks to '2, +1 at master Society, +1 at legendary Society' (a proficiency-scaled count, which is itself a second engine gap). engineNote claim (b) — that a background-granted feat never renders a sub-choice picker — is CORRECT and verified (Builder.tsx:990-1004 renders it as a read-only 'skill feat · granted' block; the sub-choice pickers at Builder.tsx:1172-1191 and 1265-1285 are all gated on `picked`).
